selectionRules: The opening uses four landmarks. Other main preference panels have at most two, with lesser-known specific counterexamples.
Ranking pairs from one task are dependent evidence.
WHY means a tentative explanation consistent with choices, not an internal causal reading.
Keep liking, interest, affect, self-reported recognition and stated reasons separate.
Reservations cover first preference ratings, not all visual exposure.
Country/context, era and artist selection are not personality, national identity, religion, politics or morality.
Approximate crosses on panels 5, 6 and 12 are designed comparisons with documented confounds, not causal experiments.
Original humanity means visible human-figure salience here, not virtue, kindness or humaneness.
Narrative, atmosphere and energy descriptors contain editorial judgement. Pixel palette is a property of the local reproduction, not original pigment or an emotional response.
Lesser-known culturally important works remain tradition anchors. Popularity is separate from quality and importance.

laterComparisonBriefs.roleNotes: Crowded human-scene reserve. Check lighting and figure organisation after earlier group scenes; subject, maker, setting and fame remain alternatives.
English river and literary female-figure near-match. Artist, narrative event, pose and palette differ.
Known artist with a new subject. Check the reach of a Van Gogh explanation beyond stars and sunflowers.
High-value Northern Song monumental-landscape and ink-on-silk near-match. Artist, date, composition and reproduction differ.
Animal without a dominant human figure. Pose, conflict, palette and treatment differ.
Body and social-setting check before later mythological figures. No sexual-orientation or moral inference.
Geometric treatment with a recognisable figure and hinted action; helps break abstraction from absence of narrative.
Flower still life across makers. This 1864 Monet is not the mature Water Lilies treatment.
Collaborative image of art-making gives another gathering and multiple authorship; keep Kyosai and others.
Chinese bird-and-flower subject and colour counterexample to a mountain-only sample.
Recognisable food and arranged space. Food-subject liking is not evidence of appetite or materialism.
Same-artist alternate subject and visible labour; a check across actual pictures rather than a single artist label.
Same artist, back-turned figures and large landscape. Weather, number of figures, viewpoint and palette differ.
Strong near-match: Kirchner wrestlers and Bellows boxing are both 1909 oil paintings on canvas about physical contests. Sport, palette, crowd and rendering differ.
Edo narrative painting by Katsushika Oi extends Japanese painting beyond two familiar printmakers. Bodily action and narrative knowledge remain confounded.
Precolonial Mesoamerican wall fragment adds a temporal/material contrast. No primitive-to-modern progression or single Mexican taste.
Ragamala convention links a figure to a musical mode; that history is not the participant's actual emotion.
Second Roman Egyptian funerary portrait limits a whole-tradition claim from one panel. Age, date, maker and material differ.
Sparse death scene after quiet and crowded narratives. Political and historical knowledge remain alternatives.
Same-artist architecture versus water and garden. Surface, palette, legibility and prior exposure differ.
Very sparse nonfiguration checks geometric choices. Material aging and reproduced colour are not original-pigment preference measurements.
Mythological body image extends figural comparisons. Format, era, iconography and fame differ.
Baroque narrative with visible agency. Authorship, setting, pose and story matter; no violence-endorsement inference.
Frontal figures and ambiguous social relation challenge gaze-versus-story explanations in a different setting.
Same artist with a different subject and medium. Interest in a religious image cannot establish beliefs.
Same-year Klee comparison with geometric construction and hinted action; pictorial means and density differ.
Ming landscape check. Do not collapse centuries and schools into a uniform Chinese ink taste.
Korean 1934 plant and brushwork subject broadens the mountain sample; no timeless East Asian type.
European artist in colonial Tahiti. This does not supply Indigenous Oceanic authorship.
Picture of pictures and collecting offers another object-rich scene. Reproduction resolution affects small embedded images.
Rinpa plant screen and gold ground broaden Japanese subjects and formats; original scale and photographed metallic surface differ.
Korean ten-panel mountain screen versus Chinese hanging-scroll landscapes. Small full-screen reproduction changes detail visibility.
Chinese everyday play counters a mountain-only sample. Activity, format and representation vary.
Weather with human figures; historical seasonal and poetic conventions are context, not universal emotions.
Korean animal family broadens animal imagery and Joseon subjects. Cultural meaning is context, not presumed knowledge.
